subject: Bridge-package question: mixing modules and discount impacts
messages:
From: Sophie Laurent <sophie@healthgrid.ai>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-15T09:12:00-04:00
Subject: Bridge-package question: mixing modules and discount impacts

Hi Mateo,

Quick question as we draft our procurement request — we like the Core tier for latency but only need two of the Core modules (RETRIEVE and RERANK). We also want a compact embedding pipeline from the Compact tier for cost reasons. Is there a recommended way to compose a bridge package that mixes modules across tiers?

Specifically:
- Can we pick Core compute + Compact embedding and keep a predictable unit price?
- Will the mixed setup still qualify for the volume discount ladder, or is discounting tier-based only?
- Any constraint on feature flags (e.g., advanced caching/kv sharing) if modules cross tiers?

We have an internal deadline to size the PO by EoM. Appreciate any guidance + a sample pricing sketch.

Thanks,
Sophie
Head of Platform
HealthGrid

[Attachment: initial_requirements.pdf (summary)]

From: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
To: Sophie Laurent <sophie@healthgrid.ai>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-15T12:03:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Bridge-package question: mixing modules and discount impacts

Hi Sophie — thanks for the clear note. Short answer: yes, you can combine modules from different tiers, but there are a few trade-offs we should call out up front.

High level:
- Composable packages: We support module-level composition (compute + embedding + rerank) so you can run Core inference for generation/reranking and Compact for embeddings. We’ll surface a combined SKU in the quote.
- Discounts: Volume discounts are applied at the deal level (total committed spend) not strictly by tier, so a blended discount is possible. However, certain promotional tier discounts (e.g., Core pilot credits) may not stack with blended pricing promos.
- Feature gating: Advanced runtime features (multi-model KV sharing, cross-module prefix cache) require a compatibility flag; if you mix Core + Compact we enable a cross-tier compatibility mode but it has a small performance caveat we can quantify.

Would you like a quick sketch with three scenarios: minimal bridge (2 Core modules + Compact embeddings), balanced (same throughput across modules), and throughput-optimized (Core uplift + embedding cache)? I can pull pricing_grid.xlsx and a one-page SOW draft.

If you want, I’ll loop Kimberly to confirm discounting guardrails and the recommended amortization approach for seat vs throughput credits.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0192

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-15T13:20:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Bridge-package question: mixing modules and discount impacts

Mateo — thanks for the clear framing. A couple operational notes for HealthGrid that I want to lock down before we run numbers:

1) Promotional stacking: we cannot combine a new-customer Core pilot promo with a multi-module volume commit that already uses a promotional credit. If HealthGrid wants promotional credit + blended discount, we need a written exception from Sales Ops.

2) Amortization / credits: to keep bookkeeping simple we recommend allocating commit spend into two buckets in the quote (Compute Commit / Embedding Commit). Discounts are computed on the combined bucket but we show per-bucket unit economics in the spreadsheet. This avoids surprises when they convert seats into throughput later.

3) Cross-tier features: enabling KV sharing across compact/core is allowed but must be added to the SOW as a runtime option and will add a minor engineering onboarding fee (one-time).

I’ll authorize a 10% blended discount for a first-year commit up to $350k (subject to procurement redlines). If they push for larger volume we can move to a stepped discount schedule.

Kimberly Park
Senior Sales Manager — Redwood Inference
[kimberly_park@redwood.com]

[Internal note: as long as HealthGrid is OK with the onboarding fee we can include the compatibility flag in the SOW. Will confirm with Sales Ops tomorrow.]

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-16T08:45:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Bridge-package question: mixing modules and discount impacts

Adding a product perspective and the numbers I ran locally:

Scenario A — Minimal bridge:
- 2x Core modules (generation + rerank) sized at p10 throughput
- 1x Compact embedding pipeline at p50 throughput
- Estimated blended token cost: $0.0018/token (projected)
- Expected throughput headroom: moderate; latency SLO preserved for Core ops.

Scenario B — Balanced:
- Even throughput targets across Core + Compact
- Blended token cost: $0.0020/token, better amortization on reserved capacity
- We recommend enabling embedding cache to shave embedding costs by ~25% (config opt-in).

Operational caveat: enabling cross-tier KV/prefix cache increases memory footprint on Core instances; if HealthGrid expects high concurrent context sharing we should size an extra GPU node in the Dedicated pool (one-time capacity uplift).

I attached a quick pricing_grid.xlsx with the per-scenario math and an example SOW line for the cross-tier compatibility flag.

—Karthik
Product Lead, Packaging Strategy
[karthik_iyer@redwood.com]

Sophie — attaching the sketch and SOW draft as discussed. Summary and next steps below.

Summary:
- You can compose Core compute for generation + rerank with Compact embeddings. We will present a blended SKU and apply a deal-level discount (we can confirm exact percent once you pick a scenario).
- I’m proposing Scenario B (Balanced) for HealthGrid as it gives predictable unit economics and the option to enable embedding cache.
- There is a one-time onboarding fee to enable cross-tier KV sharing; we’ve listed it in the SOW and included the capacity uplift note.

Next steps (can we do the following this week?):
1) Confirm preferred scenario (A/B) so I can finalize numbers.
2) Procurement: if HealthGrid needs promotional stacking, let us know and I’ll request an exception from Sales Ops (may add 48–72h).
3) If you want the capacity uplift included we’ll add the extra Dedicated node to the quote and reflect it in the PO.

Attachments: HealthGrid_SOW_v1.pdf (SOW stub), pricing_grid.xlsx (scenario math).

If procurement would like a short call to walk the spreadsheet I’m available tomorrow 10–11am PT.

Thanks — looking forward to finalizing.
